aspects.says: Composition raises its own edge cases: circular composition, serializable parts and deep versus shallow copies of composed state.
aspects.reason: named in passing with no worked example on the page; the view-not-copy edge of the forwarding wrapper practises the shared-state half

aspects.says: The forwarding wrapper pattern wraps any implementation of an interface and adds behaviour by delegating to it, so the wrapped object's internals cannot double-count.
A subclass that overrides methods its superclass calls internally depends on the superclass's implementation, so an InstrumentedHashSet's addAll counts every element twice.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: Composition gives a class a has-a relationship: it holds another object in a field and delegates work to it, where inheritance gives an is-a relationship.
Inheritance fits only a genuine is-a relationship with a superclass designed for extension, such as AbstractList, not a concrete class like ArrayList.
A subclass that changes the meaning of inherited methods breaks the Liskov Substitution Principle, which composition avoids.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: the Liskov Substitution Principle is practised on its own page, 8.1.3; here it is named only as a reason to compose

aspects.says: A composed object is checked with Objects.requireNonNull in the constructor, so a null delegate is refused at once.
A forwarding class must also delegate equals, hashCode and toString, or it keeps Object's identity-based versions and breaks the Set contract.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: Too many wrapper layers where plain inheritance fits add complexity without benefit.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: a design judgement: a test sees only what a class computes, never whether a wrapper layer was needed

aspects.says: Strategy, Decorator and Adapter are all built on composition and delegation.
aspects.reason: each pattern is practised on the design-pattern pages; the strategy-style stages of this page's text processor practise the composition they share

aspects.says: Records are implicitly final and cannot be extended, so they lead a design towards composition.
Behaviour composed from functional interfaces can be combined, ordered and extended at runtime without any class hierarchy.
Java lets a class extend only one class, so combining behaviour from several sources needs composition.
